(2) e2 reads whole every row FIXUP-5 changes, which is 21 rows if the applied digest matches. (3) e2 runs a script diff from F4 to the FIXUP-5 applied rows showing only E7's exact spans changed and every other row byte-identical, and e1's CONFIRM on those rows carries by that byte equality and by nothing else. (4) e2 states for each of e1's 13 MET conditions whether FIXUP-5 touched what it measured, and re-runs any that it did. (5) e2 confirms W2-006, W3-001 and W3-002 no longer stand at RETURN. Deciding runs: B3 (E4 s2_conditions[6]) by e2's read of fixtures_tf4.result.json for TF-4's eleven plants with the sweep on the FIXUP-5 rows; B4 (s2_conditions[7]) by e2's read of fixtures_tf5.result.json and mutants_tf5.result.json with the same sweep; B7 (s2_conditions[10]) by a script comparing confidence on every row from draft_rows_fixup2_applied.jsonl to the FIXUP-5 rows; B8 (s2_conditions[11]) by a script field diff over the same two files against every licensed span applied between them, with the RP and SBLGNT slices recomputed. A change no pinned licence covers leaves B8 not MET. e1 and e2 together stand as the boss record only when every condition is MET and no row stands at RETURN.
rulings.reason: The four clauses failed for want of named files, not for a finding, so naming and pinning them cures that. With step (3) every final row's bytes are read whole by e1 or e2, and I read that as meeting the clause for the boss. That reading is mine; it goes to Fable's end review with the rest of this file.
